newsitem.title: GERMANY: Debis may raise stake in Cap Gemini - paper.
newsitem.headline: Debis may raise stake in Cap Gemini - paper.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Interservices AG (Debis), the financial services arm of Germany's Daimler-Benz AG, may increase its stake in French software house Cap Gemini SA from 24.4 percent to a majority holding, a German newspaper reported on Friday.
A decision will be taken this year, the newspaper said.
It quoted Debis management board chairman Klaus Mangold as saying that two changes in U.S. law which come into effect in May could pave the way for a stake increase, the report said,

Mangold was also reported as saying that Debis would have to pay four billion marks to buy all the remaining shares in Cap Gemini but could resell some of the shares as long as it retained a majority.
If Debis bought all the outstanding shares "one would have to find ways to get back to a sensible majority from our point of view," Mangold was quoted as saying.
Reselling the shares would not pose a fundamental problem, the paper said.
"In Europe and the U.S. there is enormous demand at present for shares in information technology companies," it quoted Mangold as saying.
Raising the stake in Cap Gemini to 50 percent plus one share would cost about one billion marks, Mangold said. "In that case we would need help with financing from the group," Mangold said.
But he added that thoughts about a stake increase had not progressed that far.

Under the current version of the U.S. Bank-Holding-Company-Act, Daimler, which is listed in the U.S., would not be able to increase its stake in Cap Gemini, which has strong activities in the U.S., beyond 25 percent, the paper said.
Daimler's activities are restricted under the law because Deutsche Bank AG holds a 24.4 percent stake in it, the paper said. But the law is being amended to allow exceptions, it added.
"That could make things easier for us to a certain extent," Mangold said.
